title: Grain Clerk Training Note: How Grade Is Settled on a Load Taken Under Grain Marketing Contracts
content:
Grade on Grain Marketing Contracts is settled on the readings taken at unload and never renegotiated afterwards on the member's recollection of the load. The note below answers the points of judgement that arise on a grade line.

**What is discounted, and on what basis.** Test weight below the base for the commodity is discounted for each whole pound below base, part pounds being rounded down in the member's favour. Foreign material above the free tolerance is discounted for each percentage point above it, part points counted proportionally. Damage is not discounted point by point but by the band it falls in, taking the discount of the lowest band whose ceiling the reading does not exceed. A load whose damage reaches the rejection level is refused at the pit and no ticket is written for it at all.

**Do the three stack, or is the worst taken?** They stack. A load can carry a test weight, a foreign material and a damage discount at once, and the discounts are added rather than the worst one taken.

**How is money rounded?** Money on a grade line is rounded half up to the cent. Test weight is rounded down to a whole pound; foreign material points are taken proportionally rather than rounded.

**How many grade lines may one ticket carry?** Exactly one quality discount line is carried per scale ticket, so a reweigh or a recheck adjusts the existing line rather than adding a second one. The line is correlated to the ticket by the ticket number, and what distinguishes one line from another on the same ticket is the day it was posted and the amount it carries.

**What does a grade line come to?** The grade discount taken on a ticket is the net bushels on that ticket multiplied by the sum of two rates: the test weight shortfall in whole pounds below base multiplied by the per-pound test weight discount, and the foreign material above the free tolerance in percentage points multiplied by the per-point foreign material discount. That figure is rounded to the cent.

**A hypothetical load.** On a hypothetical ticket carrying 1,000 net bushels, a test weight two and a half pounds below base counts as two whole pounds, and foreign material one and a half points above the free tolerance counts as one and a half points. At the posted rates of 0.02 per pound and 0.015 per point, the per-bushel discount is 0.0625, and the grade line comes to 62.50.

## Clause no longer in force

One clause of this rule is **no longer in force** and is carried here only so that no reader applies it:

> "Grade discounts are taken against the price of the bushels on that ticket and appear on the settlement statement the bushels are drawn onto; they are never taken a second time when the bushels are later priced."
